severity_note: higher than the review's medium: every coarsening level of every parallel ordering/partitioning (dgord, dgpart, SCOTCH_dgraphOrder/Map) passes through these allocations, and one process out of memory hangs the whole job instead of failing; 20 of the 23 injected allocations hung
location_7_0_17: src/libscotch/dgraph_match_sync_coll.c:121-124 (4P-int work array per pass); dgraph_coarsen.c:883-886 (thrdtab, 'TODO: cleaner exit'), 1090-1101 (agreement on the coarse arrays compiled out), 604-608 (BuildSeq hash table), 724-729 (BuildThr per-thread tables) and 1251-1254/1263-1266 (return before the final dgraphAllreduceMaxSum l.1280)

first_pass_critique: Status and reproduction right (it found PS-DGR-1 on the way). Its preferred option 1 ('hoist into the Init functions') is right in spirit but it adds a new DgraphMatchData field and 4P ints for an array that already exists twice: the coarse graph's procrcvtab/procsndtab and the coarsening count arrays, which the maintainer's own dgraphCoarsenBuildColl() uses with the comment 'TRICK: use coarse graph procrcvtab and procsndtab' (alt/DGR-13-C is its diff). It also left the Build sites as 'sketch only' and did not see that the final dgraphAllreduceMaxSum can carry the error flag (its option 3 sentinel idea, but on the reduction, where no sentinel convention is needed).
